title: Robust Inverse Framework using Knowledge-guided Self-Supervised Learning: An application to Hydrology

problem.claim: Accurate broad-scale streamflow models remain difficult to build because dominant hydrologic processes vary and are best captured by process-related basin characteristics.

gap.claim: Existing basin characteristics contain noise and uncertainty that adversely affect model performance.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Knowledge-guided Self-Supervised Learning inverse framework that extracts system characteristics from driver and response data.
The framework achieves robust performance when characteristics are corrupted or missing.
The framework is evaluated for streamflow modeling using the CAMELS hydrology benchmark dataset.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the proposed KGSSL inverse framework as novel and first-of-its-kind.

author_reported_evidence.claim: KGSSL outperforms the baseline by 16% when predicting missing characteristics.
When static characteristics are unknown, characteristics inferred by KGSSL improve forward-modeling performance by 35% over a standard baseline.

narrative_sequence.summary: Machine learning is achieving state-of-the-art performance in environmental applications including streamflow prediction.
Broad-scale streamflow modeling remains challenging because hydrologic processes vary across basins and depend on process-related characteristics.
Noise and uncertainty in existing basin characteristics reduce model performance.
The authors propose KGSSL to infer system characteristics from input and output data, with robustness to corrupted or missing characteristics.
On the CAMELS benchmark, KGSSL reportedly improves missing-characteristic prediction and forward modeling relative to baselines.

source_observation.claim: A knowledge-guided self-supervised inverse framework infers system characteristics from driver and response data and remains robust to corrupted or missing characteristics.

interpretation.claim: Combining domain knowledge with self-supervised inverse learning may help recover useful latent or static characteristics under incomplete or noisy observations.

application.claim: This approach may be applicable to environmental modeling settings where process characteristics are noisy, missing, or difficult to measure directly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported improvements generalize beyond the hydrology setting and CAMELS dataset.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the KGSSL architecture, training procedure, or incorporated knowledge constraints.
The abstract does not define the baseline methods or evaluation protocol.
The abstract does not report uncertainty estimates, statistical significance, or results beyond the CAMELS streamflow setting.
